standardized.notes: ITU development history identifies the first V.42 edition as November 1988.

roles: provide standardized error-correcting procedures for duplex modems
convert asynchronous DTE data into an error-controlled synchronous modem link
support LAPM as the principal standardized link procedure while interoperating with installed compatibility procedures
error_control: HDLC-derived Link Access Procedure for Modems (LAPM) provides framing, sequence/error handling and retransmission behavior; deployed V.42 products also preserved alternate MNP compatibility.
flow_or_congestion_control: Modem buffering and link procedures interact with DTE flow control; exact V.42 parameter/state details require clause-level extraction from the 1988 text.

operations.monitoring: Product implementations expose negotiated error-control mode and diagnostics through vendor command interfaces.
operations.diagnostics: Negotiation/fallback and retransmission behavior require implementation traces and modem manuals.
operations.failure_behavior: Damaged/error frames are handled by link error-control procedures instead of being blindly exposed as a raw character stream.
operations.operator_interface: Usually surfaced through vendor modem result codes/AT commands rather than V.42 itself.

open_questions: Acquire the original November 1988 text and record exact Annex/alternate MNP wording.
Build the LAPM state machine and frame-format record.
Recover original Microcom records that explain how MNP compatibility entered the standardized ecosystem.
Capture real negotiation traces demonstrating LAPM versus MNP fallback.

sources.locator: ITU V.42 recommendation database and development history

sources.notes: Vendor manual is implementation evidence rather than the normative source.

related_artifacts.notes: V.42bis compression layered with error-controlled links

notes: V.42 is an error-control standard, not a modulation-speed standard. Keep it separate from V.32/V.34/V.90 physical modulation genealogy.
